subject.title: fix(logging): warn when configured file writes fail

question: Should upgrades intentionally reject previously accepted blank `logging.file` values and require `openclaw doctor --fix` to restore the default path?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but choosing whether a released config value becomes invalid is an operator-facing compatibility policy decision that review automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept nonblank canonical config
options.body: Merge the current validation plus doctor migration, intentionally requiring affected installations to run doctor before normal startup.

options.title: Narrow to runtime diagnostics
options.body: Keep the failed-write warning but leave blank values schema-valid, avoiding an upgrade break while retaining the existing ambiguous config contract.

options.title: Split the compatibility change
options.body: Land the warning separately and handle blank-path retirement in a maintainer-sponsored migration change with explicit release planning.

recommendation.title: Accept nonblank canonical config
recommendation.body: Merge the current validation plus doctor migration, intentionally requiring affected installations to run doctor before normal startup.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to cross-cutting logging, configuration, doctor, and upgrade decisions.
